title: Impact of Surprise Electoral Outcomes on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event Study.  
Rationale: The surprise electoral outcome is a well-defined, exogenous event that occurs at a single point in time (event‐day 0). The key objective is to measure abnormal stock‐market performance in a short window around that date, making the event-study framework the natural causal design.  
Key assumptions  
1. No confounding news affecting the whole market or specific industries in the narrow event window (−1,0,+1).  
2. The market model estimated in the pre-event estimation window (−10 to −3) correctly captures normal returns (Conditional Mean Independence).  
3. Markets are semi-strong efficient, so any causal impact materialises immediately.  

## 2. R Code
```r
#####################################################################
# Impact of Surprise Electoral Outcome on Industry CAR – Event Study
#####################################################################

# Required packages
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 1. LOAD DATA -------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s64_data.csv")

# 2. DEFINE WINDOWS --------------------------------------------------
event_day      <- 0
estimation_win <- -10:-3    # used to estimate alpha & beta
event_win1     <- -1:1      # main window  (-1,0,+1)
event_win2     <- -2:2      # robustness  (-2,-1,0,+1,+2)

# 3. ESTIMATE ALPHA & BETA PER INDUSTRY -----------------------------
betas <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% estimation_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do(tidy(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .))) %>% 
  select(stock_id, term, estimate) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>% 
  rename(alpha_hat = `(Intercept)`, beta_hat = mkt_ret)

# Merge estimated parameters back
df <- df %>% left_join(betas, by = "stock_id")

# 4. COMPUTE ABNORMAL RETURNS ---------------------------------------
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(AR = ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret))

# 5. MAIN CAR  (-1 to +1) -------------------------------------------
car_main <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win1) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# 6. ROBUSTNESS CAR  (-2 to +2) -------------------------------------
car_rob  <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win2) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_rob = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# 7. POOLED STATISTICS ----------------------------------------------
results <- car_main %>% 
  left_join(car_rob, by = "stock_id") %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean_CAR      = mean(CAR),
    t_CAR         = mean(CAR) / (sd(CAR)/sqrt(n())),
    Mean_CAR_rob  = mean(CAR_rob),
    t_CAR_rob     = mean(CAR_rob) / (sd(CAR_rob)/sqrt(n()))
  )

print("==============================================================")
print("Event Study – Industry-level Cumulative Abnormal Returns")
print(results)
print("==============================================================")

# 8. SIMPLE CHECK: MARKET-ADJUSTED RETURNS (no beta, no alpha)-------
df <- df %>% mutate(AR_simple = ret - mkt_ret)

simple_car <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win1) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_simple = sum(AR_simple)) %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean_CAR_simple = mean(CAR_simple),
    t_CAR_simple    = mean(CAR_simple) / (sd(CAR_simple)/sqrt(n()))
  )

print("Market-adjusted (beta=1) robustness:")
print(simple_car)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: A surprise pro-business electoral outcome should generate positive abnormal returns because investors revise upward the expected cash-flows or regulatory environment. I therefore expect the mean CAR in the (−1,0,+1) window to be positive, roughly +1½ % to +3 % across industries, with a t-statistic around 2–3 indicating statistical significance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Analyze stock returns before and after the election event to isolate the impact of the surprise outcome.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The unexpected election result led to a negative impact on industry-level CAR.
